pmc-10671107.title: Cumulative Incidence of All-Cause Knee Injury, Concussion, and Stress Fracture among Transgender Patients on Gender-Affirming Hormone Therapy: An Exploratory Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-10671107.creator: Emily W Miro, Eliza Taylor, Andrew Curtin, Michael G Newman, Dominik Ose, Jordan Knox
pmc-10671107.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Previous research has shown a discrepancy in incidences of knee injuries, stress fractures, and concussions between cisgender men and women. Little is known regarding the incidence of musculoskeletal injuries among patients on gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT). This retrospective cohort study examines cumulative incidence of knee injuries, concussions, and stress fracture injuries among transgender patients on GAHT at one health system from 2011–2020. Using relevant ICD-9 and 10 codes, incidences of knee injury, concussion, and stress fracture were calculated.

pmc-12735090.title: Hypoxia as a Central Regulator of Plasma Membrane Phosphohydrolase Enzymes: Possible Roles in Extracellular Phosphate Generation and Adenosine Metabolism
pmc-12735090.creator: Pedro Henrique Silva de Oliveira, Beatriz Bereda Silva-Freitas, José Roberto Meyer-Fernandes, Marco Antonio Lacerda-Abreu, Shiro Suetsugu
pmc-12735090.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This article presents a conceptual perspective proposing that hypoxia acts as a unifying regulator of plasma membrane phosphohydrolases. We propose that oxygen sensing at the cell surface integrates adenosine and phosphate metabolism to sustain tumour adaptation. Within the oxygen- and nutrient-deprived tumour microenvironment, inorganic phosphate (Pi) and adenosine function as metabolic substrates and signalling mediators that promote cell proliferation, survival, and immune evasion.
